children: Euro is near its weakest level since April 2025. Friday’s US producer-price report will test whether buyers can hold the $1.1045–$1.1050 area.
pair tested $1.1045 early Friday, a support area where a short-term descending channel and a long-term ascending channel meet.

Thursday’s low near $1.1066 is the first level to reclaim. Buyers stepped in around that price Thursday, but the bounce faded in Friday’s Asian session. A move back above $1.1066 would be the first sign that buyers are regaining ground.

A sustained break below $1.1045 would bring $1.1000 into view. That round number is the next obvious chart reference. With US inflation data due later in the session, watch where the pair trades once the initial reaction settles.
💵 Higher US yields back the dollar

A quarter-point Fed hike remains the main December expectation. Markets put the chance of a half-point increase at about 14.5%, up from zero a week earlier.
Tuesday’s hotter CPI report helped open that debate after core prices rose 0.3% for a third straight month.
🏦 Producer prices put support to the test

US producer prices are due at 8:30 a.m. ET. Consensus calls for a 0.4% monthly headline rise and a 0.3% core increase. Another upside surprise could lift short-term yields and give dollar buyers a reason to press euro-dollar below its early lows.
A softer PPI print could ease the pressure if two-year yields give back some of their gains. A recovery through $1.1066 would put Thursday’s rebound area near $1.1090 back in view.
The ECB has its own December decision to weigh. Euro-area inflation reached 4% in October, keeping a further rate increase in the conversation after the ECB held in October.
Dollar holds strong in FX trading

title: EURUSD: Euro Slumps to Long-Term Support at $1.1045, Dollar Holds Near Recent High
